nativeOutcome: One additional living-wage job placement attributable to the Center within the reporting year
decision: Publish an explicit, very-low-confidence decision estimate of approximately $168 million per 10 QALYs. The closest joint employment-and-utility randomized evidence found a 4.9-percentage-point employment gain and 0.01 incremental QALY per participant over 18 months for intensive Individual Placement and Support in adults receiving alcohol or drug treatment. Dividing those trial effects implies 0.204 QALY per additional job start only if all QALY change is assigned to the employment effect. MFI retains 10% of that ratio for population, program, mediation, and instrument transfer and then retains 50% for unknown Center placement durability, yielding 0.0102 QALY per modeled additional placement. Combined with the native $171,768 conditional placement price, the central comparison price is approximately $168 million per better life. The conditional positive-effect range is approximately $8.42 million to $11.2 billion; a true null, harm, or funding displacement remains plausible. This is a best-effort donor estimate, not a measured Center effect, verified marginal price, rank, or funding recommendation.

sourceEvidence.design: Pragmatic, multicenter randomized controlled trial of Individual Placement and Support versus treatment-as-usual employment support
sourceEvidence.population: 1,687 adults in community treatment for alcohol or drug dependence in England; 1,403 had linked employment data for the complete-case employment comparison
sourceEvidence.intervention: Up to 13 months of intensive Individual Placement and Support integrated into seven treatment centers
sourceEvidence.boundary: The trial jointly estimates intervention effects on any employment during 18 months and EQ-5D-5L QALYs; it does not establish that employment mediated the QALY gain. Participants had diagnosed substance dependence and received intensive integrated IPS. The Center serves a broader LGBTQ+ population through a different, incompletely specified service mix, so neither the trial effect nor the implied QALY-per-job ratio is directly transferable.

conditionalCostPerAdditionalPlacementUsd.basis: The native v0.1 model divides the broad FY2024 Economic Development allocation by 30 reported placements and assumes 25% are additional in the central scenario. The 10%–50% attribution cases are judgmental, not evidence estimates; the numerator includes non-employment services and is not a marginal price.

externalImpliedQalyPerAdditionalJobStart.basis: Trial incremental QALY per participant divided by the 4.9-percentage-point complete-case employment difference. This ratio is an arithmetic joint-outcome anchor, not a causal mediation estimate or a QALY weight for employment.

retainedShareForProgramPopulationAndMedi.basis: The midpoint retains 10% because the trial used intensive integrated IPS in adults with substance dependence, while the Center reports a mixed service bundle and a broad LGBTQ+ population; employment may not mediate the trial QALY gain. This is a judgment range.

retainedShareForPlacementDurability.basis: The Center reports job starts without 6- or 12-month retention, hours, benefits, or earnings. The midpoint gives half credit relative to the trial's 18-month observation window; this is a decision assumption, not measured retention.

modeledBridge.nullBoundary: The numeric range is conditional on a positive Center-attributable placement effect, a positive transferable health-utility relationship, placement durability, and donor additionality. The Center has no causal comparison or retention data; the external trial's QALY gain was not shown to be mediated by employment; individualized coaching is paused; and no marginal funding plan is published. If the Center does not change placement probability, employment produces no health-utility gain for this population, QALY change is transient or adverse, placements do not persist, or a gift displaces public or restricted funding, the impact price has no finite positive upper bound.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Center placement definition and retention
evidenceWeaknesses.why: The published 30+ count does not define wage threshold, hours, benefits, start date, duplicate people, service pathway, or 6- and 12-month retention.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Center causal placement effect
evidenceWeaknesses.why: The 25% central attribution is a decision scenario, not evidence. The Center has no concurrent comparison or baseline placement rate; null or harm remains plausible.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Employment-to-QALY mediation
evidenceWeaknesses.why: The external RCT measured both outcomes but did not show that its QALY gain was caused by additional employment. Dividing joint effects is an arithmetic anchor, not mediation evidence.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Population and intervention transfer
evidenceWeaknesses.why: The trial integrated intensive IPS with alcohol and drug treatment. The Center's broader LGBTQ+ population, baseline health, discrimination exposures, service mix, fidelity, and comparator differ.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Employment-program cost and funding room
evidenceWeaknesses.why: The numerator is the whole Economic Development allocation, including non-employment services. Government grants supplied 55% of FY2024 revenue, coaching is paused, and the next gift's capacity and displacement are unknown.

excludedBenefits: Earnings, taxes, benefits, financial stability, and employer productivity because wage, hours, retention, and counterfactual earnings are unpublished
Confidence, social connection, discrimination reduction, housing stability, and employer-side inclusion outside the transferred EQ-5D result
Youth, financial counseling, homeownership, small-business, community-event, and other Center program benefits
Family, caregiver, employer, public-budget, and community spillovers
requiredEvidence: Pre-specify the living-wage threshold, eligible cohort, service pathway, employment start, hours, benefits, and 6- and 12-month retention and earnings outcomes.
Use a randomized, phased, or credible matched comparison with complete participant flow, exposure, missing-data analysis, and a pre-specified causal estimand.
Collect EQ-5D or another preference-based utility measure at baseline and repeated follow-up; estimate employment, utility, and mediation jointly for the same participants.
Publish the employment-program budget, active-component costs, public and restricted funding, displacement rule, capacity, and dated $100K, $1M, and $10M marginal plans.
